info.title: Enterprise Architecture Core API
info.description: Implemented process and governed Enterprise Architecture decision surface. Call GET /health, then GET /ready. Authenticated architecture readers can query the bitemporal Technology Change Impact & Target-State Planner; separately authorized human approvers can approve a proposed target state; and separately authorized schedulers can bind an approved transformation to an authoritative remediation milestone without direct table or foreign-product SQL access.

get.description: Use this probe to confirm the OS process is running. Then call GET /ready before routing tenant traffic.

200.description: Process is alive. Next action: call GET /ready.

get.description: Use this probe after GET /health. A 503 means keep the instance out of the load-balancer pool until contract and database checks pass.

200.description: Dependencies are ready. Next action: keep the instance in the serving pool.

503.description: A required dependency is not ready. Next action: inspect contract_ready and database_ready, then repair that dependency.

get.summary: Decide the next action for a technology lifecycle change
get.description: Returns tenant-scoped, bitemporal EA decision evidence joining technology lifecycle impact, affected applications and capabilities, receipt-bound foreign context evidence, remediation initiative, target scenario, transformation state, and deterministic next action. The API is read-only and never promotes inferred foreign evidence to authoritative EA truth.

200.description: Decision evidence is available. Next action is carried in next_action and each decision row.

400.description: The bitemporal request is malformed or incomplete.

401.description: A current cryptographically valid Keyverse bearer is required.

403.description: The verified identity lacks an approved EA read role.

503.description: Authorization configuration or the purpose-bound EA query port is unavailable.

post.description: Commits a human-authorized target-state approval through the EA Core purpose-bound command port. The verified Keyverse identity supplies tenant and actor authority; callers cannot spoof the decision actor. The command appends authoritative transformation history and its transactional outbox event atomically. Reusing the same decision_request_id with identical meaning returns the original receipt; conflicting meaning fails closed.

200.description: The exact decision request was already committed and the immutable receipt is replayed. Next action: schedule the approved transformation.

201.description: The target state was approved and authoritative history plus outbox evidence were committed atomically. Next action: schedule the transformation.

400.description: The strict JSON command, UUIDv7 identifiers, effective time, or bounded reason is invalid.

401.description: A current cryptographically valid Keyverse bearer is required.

403.description: The verified identity lacks an approved EA target-state approval role.

503.description: Approval authorization configuration or the purpose-bound EA command port is unavailable, or the command cannot be safely committed. Keep the decision pending and refresh the target-state plan before retrying with the same decision_request_id.

post.description: Binds an already-approved authoritative transformation to one authoritative milestone of the same remediation initiative through a purpose-bound command. The verified Keyverse identity supplies tenant and actor authority; callers cannot spoof the decision actor. The schedule binding and privacy-minimized transactional outbox event commit atomically. Exact decision-request replay returns the original receipt; conflicting meaning fails closed.

200.description: The exact schedule decision was already committed and its immutable receipt is replayed. Next action: start the governed transformation execution flow.

201.description: The approved transformation was bound to its authoritative remediation milestone and outbox evidence was committed atomically. Next action: start the governed transformation execution flow.

400.description: The strict JSON command, UUIDv7 identifiers, effective time, milestone identity, or bounded reason is invalid.

401.description: A current cryptographically valid Keyverse bearer is required.

403.description: The verified identity lacks an approved EA transformation scheduling role.

503.description: Schedule authorization configuration or the purpose-bound EA command port is unavailable, or the command cannot be safely committed. Refresh the approved transformation and milestone evidence before retrying with the same decision_request_id.
